summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with cirrhosis from chronic hepatitis C and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation after a planned radiofrequency ablation was canceled due to the tumor's proximity to the IVC. Instead, a liver biopsy and fiducial seed placement were performed. Post-procedure, she had a drop in hematocrit from 32 to 25, indicating a slow bleed, likely from the biopsy site. She remained hemodynamically stable, received one unit of packed red blood cells and clotting factors, and was monitored closely. Her propranolol was held initially to avoid masking tachycardia from bleeding but was restarted when stable. She was discharged home in good condition with no active bleeding, instructions to follow up on biopsy results, and no medication changes.
